subject: Mutual action sprint — kickoff, roles, and evaluation milestones
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Brooks <ethan.brooks@stellarnet.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mutual action sprint — kickoff, roles, and evaluation milestones

Ethan / Lori,

Thanks again for the time yesterday — excited to get StellarNet's evaluation moving. Attached is a first-pass mutual action plan (RDW_MAP_v1.xlsx) that lays out a six-week sprint we typically use to validate performance, integration, and cost. High level:

- Week 0 (this week): kickoff, stakeholder alignment, environment access and data requirements
- Weeks 1–3: integration, smoke tests, and performance baselines (latency / throughput / cost)
- Weeks 4–5: model tuning, caching + batching validation, and reliability testing
- Week 6: evaluation review and decision checkpoint (go/no-go + contracting next steps)

Roles I propose to start with (please flag any changes):
- Customer eng lead: Ethan Brooks (you) — availability & test payloads, infra access
- Product / success: Lori Chen — acceptance criteria and business metrics
- Redwood SE: Karthik Iyer — integration, benchmarking, model tuning
- Redwood ML Eng: Mina Haddad — evaluation plan, quality checks, quantization guidance
- Account lead: me (Priya) — program coordination and commercial discussions

A few asks to unblock the SE work this week:
1) A sample of typical request/response payloads (anonymized) and target QPS.
2) Any IP/network restrictions (eg egress, IP allowlist) for test VMs.
3) The primary success metrics (latency p50/p95 targets, token cost threshold, correctness metrics).

Proposed kickoff times (PDT): Fri 23 Jul 10:00–10:45, Fri 23 Jul 14:00–14:45, or Mon 26 Jul 09:00–09:45. If none of these work, send two times that work for you and we'll lock it.

Attaching the MAP and a link to the living doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3cRDW-MAP-draft

Thanks — looking forward to getting the team moving.

—
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priya@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

From: Ethan Brooks <ethan.brooks@stellarnet.io>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: Lori Chen <lori.chen@stellarnet.io>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual action sprint — kickoff, roles, and evaluation milestones

Thanks Priya — appreciate the clear plan. Couple of clarifications from our side before the kickoff:

- Success criteria: primary is 95th-percentile latency <= 250ms for the short prompt use-case (average tokens ~80), and cost per 1k tokens below $X (we'll confirm target next week).
- Data: we can send anonymized payloads but have one constraint — no PII in the examples (we'll scrub).
- Compliance: we will want SOC2 evidence (audit summary or attestation) and a short list of what Redwood logs by default (retention windows).

We can do the Fri 23 Jul 10:00 slot. I'll invite our infra lead (Lori will loop in a procurement contact separately). For the kickoff, we want the SE to present the minimal architecture and a runbook for the performance test (what infra to stand up, expected VM sizes, network setup).

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2026 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual action sprint — kickoff, roles, and evaluation milestones

Nice to e-meet you, Ethan — looking forward to the kickoff tomorrow. To make the Friday session productive from an engineering standpoint, here's a short tech checklist I'll cover and items we'd like you to have available: 

1) Sample payloads (JSON) for the two main flows (short prompt ~80 tokens, long-form ~800 tokens).
2) Target QPS and expected concurrency (eg 20 QPS sustained, spiky to 200 QPS).
3) Any model preferences (open checkpoints, or do you require a specific base model family?).
4) Network constraints: outbound IP allowlist, private endpoint requirements, VPC peering needs.
5) Storage/KB access pattern if you plan to use retrieval-augmented generation (RAG).

What I will bring to the table tomorrow: an abbreviated architecture diagram, the minimal infra matrix (VM sizes / GPU profiles we recommend for baseline runs), and a short runbook for the performance tests. I'm attaching an Architectural Checklist that covers the things we'll validate in week 1.

A couple of technical notes ahead of the call:
- If your latency target is 250ms p95 for ~80 tokens, we should focus on a continuous-batching pattern with prefix caching and a 16-bit quantized runtime where possible.
- For cost experiments, we'll run a small matrix across quantized vs FP16 variants to show unit economics for the production mix.
- We'll need a test harness (k6 or locust) and a non-prod API key with scoped permissions — please work with your infra team to create that before the test window.

Quick next steps:
- Ethan: please share anonymized payloads and the QPS target by EOD tomorrow so Karthik can finalize the runbook.
- Lori: procurement will follow up on the SOC2 artifact request (we can provide the SOC2 type II summary + logging matrix).
- Karthik / Mina: prepare a 15-minute architecture + testing plan and a 15-minute evaluation metric checklist for tomorrow.

I'll own the MAP updates post-call and will circulate RDW_MAP_v1.xlsx with action owners after the meeting.

Thanks all — see you tomorrow.
